findings.issue: Reactions batch endpoint lacks message access control verification
findings.impact: GET `/reactions/batch?message_ids=...` at line 24-41 accepts arbitrary message IDs without requiring message access. Any authenticated user can query reactions on messages in private channels they don't belong to, by guessing or enumerating message UUIDs.
findings.fix: Apply access filtering: either add `requireMessageAccess` middleware for each ID or query only message IDs the user can access via channel membership join.

findings.issue: No reconnect resync mechanism — clients can miss events during disconnect
findings.impact: The frontend socket client at `apps/web/lib/socket.ts` implements reconnection with exponential backoff (lines 37-47) but has no mechanism to request missed events after reconnection. There is no `last_event_id` tracking, sequence number, or event replay endpoint. If a client disconnects for even a few seconds, messages sent during that window are permanently lost.
findings.fix: Implement event sequence tracking: (1) add a monotonically increasing sequence number to broadcast events, (2) store `last_sequence` in client localStorage, (3) on reconnect, call a `/messages/since?seq=N` endpoint to replay missed events.

findings.issue: Mixed pagination strategies — cursor-based for message list, offset-based for search
findings.impact: `GET /channels/:channelId/messages` (line 89-103) uses cursor-based pagination while search and most other list endpoints use offset-based pagination. This inconsistency forces frontend to implement two pagination strategies and complicates caching.
findings.fix: Consolidate on a single pagination strategy. Cursor-based is preferred for real-time feeds (avoids duplication on new insertions). Consider migrating search to cursor-based as well.

findings.issue: DM channels list endpoint doesn't use channel access middleware — relies solely on RLS
findings.impact: `GET /dm-channels` at line 248-255 lacks `requireChannelAccess` middleware. It uses `responseCache` but no authz middleware beyond `authenticate`, relying entirely on RLS for access control.
findings.fix: Add `requireChannelAccess` middleware for defense-in-depth, or ensure the RLS policy on `dm_channels` is correct (currently scoped to `user1_id`/`user2_id` which is sufficient).

findings.issue: Socket channel join verifies workspace membership but not private channel membership correctly
findings.impact: The `channel:join` handler at line 155-212 checks workspace membership and private channel membership, but the RLS layer doesn't enforce private channel filtering for SELECT on channels/messages. This means a malicious client could bypass the socket-level check by reading channel data directly via Supabase.
findings.fix: Fix the underlying RLS policies (see security audit) so both layers are aligned.

findings.issue: Webhook enforceBodyLimit checks spoofable Content-Length header instead of actual body size
findings.impact: The `enforceBodyLimit` middleware at line 20-29 reads `content-length` header which can be spoofed by an attacker. A request with small `content-length` header but large actual body would bypass the limit.
findings.fix: Remove the middleware and rely on Express's `express.json({ limit: '1mb' })` which enforces actual body size after parsing.

findings.issue: Socket broadcast for reactions fires asynchronously with no error propagation
findings.impact: Reaction add/remove broadcasts at lines 65-80 and 101-116 use an IIFE with empty catch blocks (`catch { // Socket broadcast best-effort }`). Failure is silently swallowed, making debugging difficult when broadcasts fail.
findings.fix: At minimum log the error: `catch (err) { logger.warn('Reaction broadcast failed', { error: String(err) }) }`

findings.issue: CRITICAL: Private channel data exposure — RLS fails to filter private channels across channels and messages tables
findings.impact: Combined channels + messages RLS gap: any workspace member can enumerate all private channels and read all messages within them. This is the single most impactful finding across all three audits. The API middleware provides partial protection but RLS is the last line of defense.
findings.fix: Fix both RLS policies to include private channel membership check. See security_principal_audit and database_integrity_migration_audit for details.

findings.issue: CRITICAL: Additive RLS insert policies bypass channel membership for message posting
findings.impact: Two insert policies on messages (`messages_insert_own` + `channel_member_insert`) are OR-combined, allowing any authenticated user to post to any channel via direct Supabase client calls.
findings.fix: Drop `messages_insert_own` policy.

findings.issue: Reactions data leaked via open RLS and unguarded batch endpoint
findings.impact: Two parallel paths leak reaction data: (1) RLS `using (true)` on reactions table, (2) batch endpoint without message access verification. Combined, any authenticated user can enumerate reactions on any message.
findings.fix: Fix RLS to scope by channel membership. Add access control to batch endpoint.

findings.issue: User presence data exposed across workspace boundaries
findings.impact: All authenticated users can see online/offline/dnd status and custom status messages for all users system-wide.
findings.fix: Scope presence visibility to workspace co-members.

findings.issue: Compliance exports visible across workspaces — lacks workspace_id column
findings.impact: Admin in workspace A can read compliance exports (messages, audit logs) belonging to workspace B. The table has no workspace scoping.
findings.fix: Add workspace_id FK and scope RLS accordingly.

findings.issue: No missed-event recovery on websocket reconnect — permanent data loss window
findings.impact: Socket reconnection has no sequence tracking or event replay. Messages, reactions, presence updates sent during disconnect are permanently lost.
findings.fix: Implement event sequence tracking with replay endpoint.

findings.issue: Announcements visible across all workspaces
findings.impact: Unlike the API endpoint which likely filters by workspace, the RLS allows any authenticated user to read all announcements.
findings.fix: Scope announcements RLS to workspace membership.

findings.issue: GDPR delete not atomic — partial deletion risk
findings.impact: 12 sequential delete calls without transaction wrapping. Partial failure leaves inconsistent user data.
findings.fix: Use transactional RPC or add compensation logic.

findings.issue: Private channel creation not restricted to admins
findings.impact: Any workspace member can create private channels. No rate limit or approval flow.
findings.fix: Restrict to admins/owners or add audit/approval.

findings.issue: Mixed pagination (cursor vs offset) across list/search endpoints
findings.impact: Inconsistent pagination forces frontend to handle two strategies, complicating cache and data reconciliation.
findings.fix: Consolidate to cursor-based pagination.

findings.issue: SQL injection sanitizer causes false positives on natural language text
findings.impact: Keywords like 'select', 'from', 'where' in natural language trigger false positive rejections on non-content fields.
findings.fix: Use syntax-aware detection instead of keyword matching.

findings.issue: CSP lacks nonce support for inline scripts
findings.impact: Future frontend work requiring inline scripts will be blocked.
findings.fix: Add nonce generation when frontend requires inline scripts.

findings.issue: Webhook body limit uses spoofable Content-Length header
findings.impact: Content-Length can be manipulated; actual body size enforcement is in express.json middleware already.
findings.fix: Remove redundant middleware.

findings.issue: Channel select RLS does not filter private channels — workspace members see all channels
findings.impact: The `channels_select_member` policy at `supabase/policies/03_channels.sql:4-14` only verifies workspace membership. Private channels (`is_private = true`) are not filtered out. Any workspace member can query all channels including private ones via Supabase client with their JWT.
findings.fix: Add private channel guard: `and (channels.is_private = false or exists (select 1 from channel_members cm where cm.channel_id = channels.id and cm.user_id = auth.uid()))`

findings.issue: Two additive RLS insert policies on messages table create a bypass for channel membership checks
findings.impact: Policy `messages_insert_own` (checks `auth.uid() = user_id`) OR `channel_member_insert` (checks channel membership) exist simultaneously. Since Supabase uses OR logic for same-table/same-operation policies, any authenticated user can insert messages into any channel by setting `user_id = auth.uid()`. This completely bypasses the channel membership requirement.
findings.fix: Remove the `messages_insert_own` policy: `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS messages_insert_own ON public.messages;`

findings.issue: Reactions SELECT policy is open to all authenticated users — no channel/workspace scoping
findings.impact: `reactions_select` at `supabase/policies/06_reactions.sql:5-7` is `using (true)`. Any authenticated user can enumerate reactions on any message, including messages in private channels. This leaks engagement patterns.
findings.fix: Add channel membership check via message join: scope to messages in channels the user can access.

findings.issue: user_presence SELECT policy is open to all authenticated users across all workspaces
findings.impact: The `user_presence` select policy uses `using (true)`, allowing any authenticated user to see the online status and custom status of every user in the system, regardless of workspace membership.
findings.fix: Scope presence visibility to users who share at least one workspace.

findings.issue: Compliance exports table has no workspace_id column — cross-workspace data exposure via RLS
findings.impact: The `compliance_exports` table lacks a `workspace_id` column. The SELECT policy allows any workspace admin/owner to read ALL rows. An admin in workspace A can see compliance exports generated for workspace B. Exports may contain sensitive message content and audit data.
findings.fix: Add `workspace_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id)` column. Update the SELECT policy to filter by workspace membership with admin role.

findings.issue: Announcements SELECT policy is `using (true)` — all authenticated users see all announcements
findings.impact: The `announcements_select` policy allows any authenticated user to read all announcements across all workspaces. Announcement content may be workspace-sensitive.
findings.fix: Scope to workspace membership: `exists (select 1 from workspace_members wm where wm.workspace_id = announcements.workspace_id and wm.user_id = auth.uid())`

findings.issue: Channels INSERT policy does not restrict private channel creation to admins
findings.impact: The `channels_insert_member` policy at `supabase/policies/03_channels.sql:18-27` allows any workspace member to create channels, including private channels. This enables unauthorized private channel creation with no admin oversight.
findings.fix: Restrict private channel creation to workspace admins/owners, or add a rate limit / approval flow.

findings.issue: Migration includes data-seeding operations (INSERT ... SELECT) that may lock large tables
findings.impact: Lines 87-101 run `INSERT INTO sidebar_categories SELECT DISTINCT ... FROM workspace_members` which scans the entire`workspace_members` table. On a production database with thousands of members, this can cause long-running locks and table bloat.
findings.fix: Move seeding to a separate post-deploy script or application-level migration that runs in batches.

findings.issue: Message select RLS does not filter private channels
findings.impact: Same root cause as the channels RLS gap — messages in private channels are exposed through the messages SELECT policy which only checks workspace membership.
findings.fix: Scope messages SELECT to include private channel membership check via join to channels + channel_members.

findings.issue: Private channel data exposed via channels select RLS — no private channel filtering
findings.impact: Any workspace member can list ALL channels including private ones. The `channels_select_member` policy only checks workspace membership, not whether the user is a member of private channels. Combined with the messages RLS gap, this exposes private channel names and content to all workspace members.
findings.fix: Add private channel membership check to `channels_select_member`: `and (channels.is_private = false or exists (select 1 from channel_members cm where cm.channel_id = channels.id and cm.user_id = auth.uid()))`
findings.exploitability: High — any workspace member can enumerate private channels and read their messages via the API

findings.issue: Conflicting RLS insert policies on messages table — `messages_insert_own` allows posting to ANY channel
findings.impact: Two insert policies exist on `messages`: `messages_insert_own` (checks `auth.uid() = user_id`) and `channel_member_insert` (checks channel membership). Supabase OR-combines same-operation policies, so any authenticated user can insert messages into ANY channel by setting `user_id` to their own ID. The API middleware prevents this but direct Supabase client calls bypass it.
findings.fix: Drop `messages_insert_own` policy: `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS messages_insert_own ON public.messages;` The `channel_member_insert` policy is sufficient and correct.
findings.exploitability: High — any authenticated user with direct Supabase access can post to any channel

findings.issue: Reactions RLS SELECT is `using (true)` — any authenticated user sees ALL reactions
findings.impact: The `reactions_select` policy allows any authenticated user to see all reactions across the system, including on messages in private channels they don't have access to. This leaks engagement patterns and channel membership information.
findings.fix: Add workspace/channel membership check: scope `reactions_select` to messages in channels the user can access, e.g. via `exists (select 1 from messages m join channels ch on ch.id = m.channel_id join workspace_members wm on wm.workspace_id = ch.workspace_id where m.id = reactions.message_id and wm.user_id = auth.uid())`
findings.exploitability: Medium — reaction data is low-sensitivity but can reveal private channel activity

findings.issue: Reactions batch endpoint lacks message access control
findings.impact: The `GET /reactions/batch?message_ids=...` endpoint at `apps/api/src/modules/reactions/routes.ts:24-41` accepts arbitrary message IDs and returns reactions without verifying user access. This allows enumerating reactions on messages in private channels.
findings.fix: Add `requireMessageAccess` middleware to the batch endpoint, or filter by message IDs the user can access.
findings.exploitability: Medium — requires brute-forcing message IDs but no rate limit on this endpoint

findings.issue: Compliance exports RLS lacks workspace scoping — cross-workspace admin data leak
findings.impact: The `compliance_exports_select` policy allows any workspace admin/owner to see ALL compliance exports across all workspaces. The table has no `workspace_id` column. Exports may contain sensitive message/audit data.
findings.fix: Add `workspace_id` column to `compliance_exports` and scope the SELECT policy to admin/owner of the matching workspace.
findings.exploitability: Medium — requires admin role in any workspace

findings.issue: user_presence RLS SELECT is `using (true)` — all authenticated users see all presence data
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can see the online/away/dnd status and custom status of all users across workspaces. This leaks user activity patterns.
findings.fix: Scope presence visibility to users sharing a workspace: add `exists (select 1 from workspace_members wm1 join workspace_members wm2 on wm1.workspace_id = wm2.workspace_id where wm1.user_id = user_presence.user_id and wm2.user_id = auth.uid())`
findings.exploitability: Low — presence is generally public in chat apps but still a privacy concern

findings.issue: GDPR account deletion uses sequential deletes without transaction wrapping
findings.impact: The GDPR delete handler at line 260-276 runs 12 sequential `supabase.from(...).delete().eq(...)` calls without wrapping in a transaction. A failure mid-way leaves orphaned data (e.g., consent logs deleted but messages not, or user record remaining with no memberships).
findings.fix: Use Supabase RPC or a server-side function to execute all deletes atomically, or implement a compensation mechanism on failure.
findings.exploitability: Low — requires authenticated user deleting own account

findings.issue: Webhook retries use in-process setTimeout — lost on server restart
findings.impact: Webhook delivery retries at lines 405-409 use `setTimeout()` which does not survive process restarts or crashes. Failed deliveries with retries pending are lost if the server restarts.
findings.fix: Use persistent scheduling via BullMQ (existing worker infrastructure) or a database-based retry queue with cron-based processor.
findings.exploitability: Low — webhook deliveries are best-effort but the expectation is reliable delivery

findings.issue: Input sanitizer SQL injection patterns cause false positives on legitimate message content
findings.impact: The SQL injection patterns at line 17-21 match common English words like `select`, `from`, `where`, `insert`, `update`, `delete` occurring in normal message text. The `content` field is exempt but other string fields are not, potentially blocking legitimate input.
findings.fix: Use a more targeted SQL injection detection approach: check for SQL syntax anomalies rather than keyword presence, or only apply to fields where SQL injection is a realistic threat (e.g., channel names, workspace slugs).
findings.exploitability: N/A — this is a usability issue, not an exploit

findings.issue: CSP policy lacks nonce/hash support for inline scripts
findings.impact: The Content-Security-Policy header uses `script-src 'self'` without nonce or hash support. If any inline scripts need to execute (e.g., in frontend rendering), they will be blocked.
findings.fix: If the application ever needs inline scripts, add nonce generation to the middleware and pass nonces through response locals. For now, this is acceptable since the API server doesn't serve HTML.
findings.exploitability: N/A — informational for future frontend work

findings.fix: Add mobile tab bar or dropdown selector for admin sub-pages on screens <768px

findings.issue: Search-bar missing aria-activedescendant on autocomplete input

findings.issue: Docker images use :latest tags without SHA pinning — cannot trace which version is deployed

findings.issue: No automated rollback trigger in CI/CD if deploy fails health checks

findings.file: apps/web (no feature flag system exists at all)

findings.issue: No rollback runbook in docs — operators have no documented procedure
findings.impact: Operator uncertainty during incident increases MTTR
findings.fix: Write rollback runbook covering detection, DB rollback, image revert, verification, communication

findings.issue: No post-deploy smoke test in CI to verify deployment health
findings.impact: Deploy failures may go undetected until users report them

findings.issue: No forward-fix strategy documented for irreversible data migrations

findings.issue: No Docker healthcheck directives in compose for web or api services
findings.impact: Caddy may route traffic to unhealthy containers during deploy
findings.fix: Add healthcheck to web and api services in docker-compose.prod.yml

findings.issue: No documented verification process for Supabase backup restorability
findings.impact: Backup existence does not guarantee restorability
findings.fix: Document weekly backup status check and quarterly restore test in runbook

findings.issue: No communication template for rollback incidents
findings.impact: Ad-hoc communication during incident may omit key details
findings.fix: Create rollback communication template with sections: status, impact, ETA, what changed

findings.issue: Deploy workflow doesn't capture image SHA256 digest for traceability
findings.impact: Cannot verify exact image running in production
findings.fix: Store pushed image digest in workflow summary or deployment environment variable

findings.issue: API /health endpoint returns status but not deployed version/commit SHA

findings.issue: No release notes or changelog diff generated in deploy workflow

findings.issue: Secrets written to .env file via heredoc in SSH script — exposed in CI logs if script fails
findings.impact: If the SSH step fails or is debugged, ALL production secrets (Supabase keys, VAPID keys, LiveKit keys) are visible in plaintext in CI logs
findings.fix: Pass secrets to the droplet via environment variables or GitHub Actions secrets injection at compose time; use docker compose --env-file with GH secret masking

findings.issue: Secrets written to .env file via heredoc with conditional injection — potential secrets leakage in logs
findings.impact: Development secrets visible in CI logs if debug enabled or SSH command errors
findings.fix: Use docker compose environment variables or GH Actions secrets injection instead of heredoc; set secrets only at container runtime

findings.issue: No path filtering on push to main — triggers full deploy on any file change
findings.impact: Documentation or config changes trigger expensive Terraform provision + Docker build + deploy cycle unnecessarily

findings.issue: Platform workflow runs pwsh script from automation dir — no input validation or scope limiting
findings.impact: Any workflow_dispatch caller can execute arbitrary pwsh scripts with GITHUB_TOKEN that has packages:write scope

findings.issue: No explicit artifact retention period set for test-results and coverage artifacts
findings.impact: Artifacts retained indefinitely by default, consuming GH Actions storage quota

findings.issue: Governance workflow has no explicit permissions block (inherits default write-all)
findings.impact: GITHUB_TOKEN has more permissions than needed, potential supply chain risk
findings.fix: Add explicit permissions: contents: read at the workflow level

findings.issue: No CI-compatible auth fixture — all E2E tests skip without test-signin.json

findings.fix: Create test user via Supabase Admin API in CI setup, or mock Supabase auth. Add CI secrets for test credentials.

findings.issue: No WebSocket reconnection E2E test exists
findings.impact: Reconnection logic (banner, auto-reconnect, message delivery after reconnect) is untested end-to-end

findings.issue: File upload E2E test skipped without test-signin.json — never runs in CI

findings.issue: No E2E tests for permission-denied or error states

findings.issue: Only 2 integration tests exist — both for health endpoints only

findings.issue: Visual snapshot tests exist but are not integrated into CI pipeline
findings.impact: Visual regressions go undetected in CI — no baseline comparison

findings.issue: Chaos tests are shell scripts with no CI integration or runner
findings.impact: Resiliency coverage is only manual — no automated validation
findings.fix: Integrate chaos tests with CI: run api-crash.sh and verify reconnection and graceful degradation

findings.issue: k6 load tests exist but are only on schedule/manual, not in CI on push
findings.impact: Performance regressions go undetected until scheduled load test run

findings.issue: No accessibility E2E tests — no axe-core or pa11y integration
findings.impact: Accessibility regressions only caught by manual audit — no automated regression detection

findings.issue: No offline/online state E2E tests
findings.impact: Offline UX (queued messages, reconnection banner, retry logic) is untested
findings.fix: Use Playwright context.route interception to simulate network failures and offline state

findings.issue: Low component unit test coverage — only one __tests__ directory exists
findings.impact: Component-level regressions may slip through
findings.fix: Set minimum 30% coverage threshold for new components; add tests for state-heavy components

findings.issue: E2E tests use fixed timeouts without smart async waiting for WebSocket/optimistic UI
findings.impact: Tests may fail intermittently in CI due to timing issues
findings.fix: Use waitForResponse API interceptors for async operations instead of fixed timeouts

findings.issue: Visual snapshot tests exist only for login page — no empty-state snapshots
findings.impact: Visual regressions in empty states go undetected
findings.fix: Add snapshot tests for empty states: no messages, no channels, no search results

findings.issue: No API integration tests for search, notifications, reactions, or admin endpoints
findings.impact: Backend search, notification, and admin logic is untested
findings.fix: Add integration tests for search API, notification preferences CRUD, and admin endpoints

findings.issue: No backup volume configuration or backup service defined for production data
findings.impact: Redis data and Caddy certs have no automated backup; loss of volumes = data loss
findings.fix: Add automated backup volume to production compose or document manual backup procedure

findings.issue: Dev environment has no explicit mem_limit on services unlike production
findings.impact: Dev environment may over-consume droplet resources, masking OOM issues in production
findings.fix: Add matching mem_limit values to dev compose for api (192m), worker (128m), web (256m), redis (64m), caddy (64m)

findings.issue: Worker healthcheck port (4100) not exposed in Dockerfile EXPOSE or compose ports
findings.impact: Health check works via internal network but container metadata incomplete
findings.fix: Add EXPOSE 4100 to worker Dockerfile for consistency

findings.issue: Production compose uses :latest tag as fallback; deploy overrides to SHA but :latest not uniquely pinned
findings.impact: Manual compose up could pull stale images if deploy script not run
findings.fix: Remove :latest defaults from production compose; require explicit SHA tag via .env

findings.issue: Dev compose uses :dev tag fallback; deploy pulls SHA tag and retags to :dev — potential race
findings.impact: Race condition between build-push completing and deploy pulling :dev before retag
findings.fix: Use SHA tag directly in dev compose via WEB_IMAGE env var, remove :dev fallback

findings.issue: Dev LiveKit config uses localhost for TURN domain while prod uses DOMAIN variable
findings.impact: Dev TURN may not work correctly for external clients testing WebRTC
findings.fix: Use ${DOMAIN:-localhost} for dev LiveKit TURN domain matching prod pattern

findings.issue: No documented policy tier inheritance hierarchy; 4 standalone policy files with no parent chain
findings.impact: Policy changes must be duplicated across files; risk of drift between dev/rc/prod policies
findings.fix: Define base policy defaults in a gate-policy.base.json with per-tier overrides; document inheritance chain in README

findings.issue: Hotfix policy file exists but no documented compensating controls or post-hotfix validation requirements
findings.impact: Hotfix path could become permanent bypass; no mandatory post-mortem or re-validation after hotfix
findings.fix: Add compensating controls section: mandatory peer review, 24h post-mortem, re-apply full gate within 7 days

findings.issue: Governance workflow is a thin wrapper calling external pwsh script with no audit trail of policy decisions
findings.impact: Policy evaluation results not captured as deploy artifacts; no traceability for compliance
findings.fix: Add policy evaluation output to workflow logs and upload as build artifact; capture decision summary

findings.issue: No documented mapping between environments and policy tiers (which policy applies to which workflow/branch)
findings.impact: Operators unclear which gate policy applies to deploy-development vs deploy-production vs hotfix flows
findings.fix: Add workflow-to-policy mapping table in policy directory README or docs/runbooks/release-process.md

findings.issue: No verified per-item ok/error result pattern in bulk endpoints — likely single-status responses
findings.impact: Partial bulk failures appear as full successes to the client; user sees fake success toast on half-failed writes
findings.fix: Audit all POST/PATCH/PUT endpoints that accept arrays; return { results: [{ ok: boolean, error?: string }] } per item

findings.issue: No systematic pattern for displaying partial-failure toasts from bulk API responses
findings.impact: Users not alerted about individual item failures in batch operations
findings.fix: Create a BulkOperationResult component that displays success count vs failure count with details

findings.issue: Each processor has its own AbortSignal.timeout(30s) but no centralized timeout wrapper in task execution
findings.impact: Inconsistent timeout enforcement across processors; new processors may forget timeout handling
findings.fix: Create a createTaskWrapper utility in worker that enforces per-task timeout, retry, and error handling consistently

findings.issue: Circuit breaker status changes logged but not exported as Prometheus metrics
findings.impact: No monitoring/alerting on circuit breaker state; open circuit not visible until users report failures
findings.fix: Export circuit breaker state (open/closed/half-open) as prometheus gauge per breaker name

findings.issue: HTTP client retry uses linear backoff (retryDelay * attemptNum) not exponential
findings.impact: Thundering herd on retry for concurrent requests; less effective than exponential backoff with jitter
findings.fix: Implement exponential backoff with jitter: delay = min(baseDelay * 2^attempt + random(0, jitter), maxDelay)

findings.issue: No circuit breaker found wrapping Supabase admin client calls despite circuit-breaker utility existing
findings.impact: Supabase outage causes cascading API failures without circuit breaker protection
findings.fix: Wrap getSupabaseAdmin calls in circuit breaker using the existing executeWithCircuitBreaker utility

findings.issue: No .dockerignore found in repo root or app directories — entire context sent to Docker daemon
findings.impact: Slower builds, larger image cache, risk of leaking .env or node_modules into build context
findings.fix: Create .dockerignore in each app directory or repo root excluding node_modules, .git, .env, dist, coverage

findings.issue: Worker Dockerfile has no HEALTHCHECK directive
findings.impact: Docker daemon cannot determine worker container health; compose uses external API health instead
findings.fix: Add HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 CMD wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:4100/healthz || exit 1

findings.issue: LiveKit image uses :latest tag without SHA pinning
findings.impact: Unpredictable version pulls across deployments; no reproducible builds for WebRTC server
findings.fix: Pin livekit/livekit-server to specific SHA digest or semver tag in production compose

findings.issue: Base images use 'node:22-alpine' without SHA digest pinning
findings.impact: Non-reproducible builds — node:22-alpine tag can change without notice
findings.fix: Pin base images to SHA256 digest: node:22-alpine@sha256:<specific_digest>

findings.issue: Dev Caddyfile lacks static asset caching rules present in prod Caddyfile.prod
findings.impact: Static assets in dev not cached with immutable headers, but may cause minor difference vs prod behavior
findings.fix: Add @static handle to dev Caddyfile matching prod patterns for consistency

findings.issue: Dev worker healthcheck uses 'kill -0 1' instead of proper HTTP health check like prod
findings.impact: Dev healthcheck only checks process existence, not actual worker readiness; misses Redis connectivity failures
findings.fix: Replace with proper HTTP health check: test: ['CMD', 'wget', '-q', '--spider', 'http://localhost:4100/healthz']

findings.issue: Dev example missing DOMAIN and ENVIRONMENT variable placeholders present in deploy scripts
findings.impact: Operators may not know DOMAIN and ENVIRONMENT variables are expected
findings.fix: Add DOMAIN=mainecybertech.us and ENVIRONMENT=development to .env.devremote.example

findings.issue: Prod example missing DOMAIN and ENVIRONMENT variable placeholders present in deploy scripts
findings.impact: Operators may not know DOMAIN and ENVIRONMENT variables are expected

findings.impact: Unhandled errors in those sections show React crash screen instead of friendly error UI
